Order 
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

02. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 02.05.2011 passed in MACC No.96/2010 by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, District Jhabua whereby a total sum of Rs.3,55,000/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, District Jhabua
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 03. As per the appellants, on 23.06.2010, Ratan Singh, husband of appellant No.1, father of appellants No.2 to 5 and son of appellant No.6 was going on his motorcycle on Indore - Ahmdabad road.

When he reached Gram Mod, respondent No.1 drove Tanker bearing registration No.GJ-06-BV-7974 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motorcycle NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9614 2 MA-2125-2011 as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment but eventually expired.
04. The appellants thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.17,50,000/- to them by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded Smt.Manju And 5 Ors. vs Mohd.Jamil And 2 Ors. on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56116436/
1 compensation to the appellants as aforesaid.

entities.text: Smt.Manju And 5 Ors. vs Mohd.Jamil And 2 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 05. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the income of the deceased which has been assessed at Rs.2,500/- per month by the Claims Tribunal is inordinately low.

From the evidence on record, it has been proved that the deceased was working and even if he had to be taken to be a semi- skilled worker, then also his income ought to have been assessed appropriately.
It is further submitted that the future prospects of rise in income which are mandatorily required to be taken into consideration have not been taken.
It is also submitted that no amount has been awarded to the appellants for filial consortium which in view of various decisions of the Apex Court deserves to be awarded.
The amount awarded to the appellants under the other heads is also inadequate.
It is hence submitted that the amount of compensation awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.

06. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company has submitted that there is absolutely no evidence available on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9614 3 MA-2125-2011 record to show that the deceased was in any employment.
The documents which have been produced by the appellants in that regard and their statements before the tribunal are wholly insufficient for the purpose of proving his income.

It is also submitted that filial consortium has been made awardable only in the year 2017 with the rider of 10% increase for every three years meaning thereby that if the same has to be awarded for an accident prior to 2017, then reduction at the rate of 10% for every three years would also have to be made for the previous years.
It is further submitted that in this appeal, the requisite amount of Court fee has not been paid by the appellants hence they do not deserve to be awarded interest for the entire period.

07. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
08.
In their statement before the tribunal, the appellants had stated that the deceased was working as a driver.
A certificate (Exhibit P/8) of the previous employer of the driver was also brought on record by them wherein it was stated that he was being paid Rs.5,000/- per month.
This is of a period just prior to the date of the accident.
Even though the employer has not been examined before the tribunal but from the evidence it is evident that the deceased was at least a semi-skilled worker.
He hence could not have been taken to be wholly unemployed and his income assessed at a meager sum of Rs.100/- per day.

In view of the guidelines which were applicable at the time of death of the deceased, his income deserves to be taken at Rs.4,275/-
per month.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9614 4 MA-2125-2011 09.

In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, 2017 (16) SCC 680 the filial, spousal and parental consortium has to be awarded at the rate of Rs.40,000/- per claimant.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been elaborated that for every three years a rise of 10% would have to be taken.

The judgment nowhere states that the same would only be Smt.Manju And 5 Ors. vs Mohd.Jamil And 2 Ors. on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56116436/
2 prospective in nature but would also be retrospective.

entities.text: Smt.Manju And 5 Ors. vs Mohd.Jamil And 2 Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same would be applicable to all pending cases also which pendency could be before the claims tribunal or in an appeal.

At the time when the said judgment came to be pronounced this appeal before this Court was pending hence the said judgment has to be applied in full force regardless of the fact that the accident took place prior to the filing of the appeal.
The appellants are six in number hence each of them is entitled for award of filial consortium to them in the sum of Rs.40,000/- i.e. Rs.2,40,000/- each.

10. The amount which the appellants are entitled for on account of loss of dependency would hence be Rs.4,275/- per month + 40% for future prospects of rise in income which would be Rs.5,985/-
per month.
The dependency of 1/4th taken and the multiplier of 15 applied by the claims tribunal is correct.
The amount which the appellants would be entitled for under this head would hence be Rs.8,08,020/-.
For consortium they are entitled for award of a sum of Rs.2,40,000/-.
For loss of estate and funeral expenses, they deserve to be awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/-.

11. The appellants are entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.10,78,020/- to them by way of compensation, whereas the claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9614 5 MA-2125-2011 Tribunal has erred in awarding them a sum of Rs.3,55,000/- only.
The appellants are hence held entitled for enhancement in the amount of compensation in the sum of Rs.7,23,020/-.

12. The appellants would be entitled for interest on the said enhanced amount of Rs.7,23,020/- from the date of filing of the claim application till 01-08-2013 when they were directed to pay Court fee at the same rate as awarded by the claims tribunal.
However, it is observed that initially the appellants had not paid any Court fee on this appeal and had only furnished an undertaking.
A sum of Rs.7,500/- by way of Court fee was paid by them on 10.07.2013.
The remaining Court fee of Rs.12,500/- was paid by them on 16.12.2019.

The appellants would hence be entitled for interest at the same rate as awarded by the claims tribunal from 01-08-2013 up to 16-09-2019 on the proportionate enhanced amount which would correspond to the Court fee paid by them.
Thereafter they would be entitled to the said interest up to the date of payment.
The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Smt.Manju And 5 Ors. vs Mohd.Jamil And 2 Ors. on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56116436/
